headline: A Business Insider writer agrees with a viral post that people want AI agents to anticipate their needs, not just follow instructions.
score_reason: Pool score kept at the floor: opinion essay.
importance_line: It captures what everyday users want from AI agents, anticipation rather than instructions, which matters to busy families, with the doubt that it is one writer's opinion built on a gendered joke.
summary: Business Insider's essay answers a post that went viral earlier this week by marketing entrepreneur and podcaster Sonia Baschez, who said Silicon Valley keeps building AI agents like "a husband" that only do assigned tasks when she wants "a wife" that anticipates her needs. The writer agrees but says agents such as Muse still need step-by-step instructions, and admits the metaphor leans on gendered stereotypes.
notes: Opinion essay; reply story: it answers Baschez's viral post earlier in the week, which we did not read and did not carry earlier.
